alignments.note: Postpositive δέ realized by the opening And.
Rule 86: a participle carries subordination, so the supplied when and subject he are its helpers; head on saw.
Reported speech with an English complementizer written, so the conjunction is aligned to it.
The expressed copula keeps the supplied anticipatory subject it; the ASV's two words for ἀρεστόν ἐστιν are divided one to each token.
The predicate adjective is what pleased realizes. Giving it was pleased whole to the adjective and leaving ἐστιν unrepresented remains defensible; the split kept here follows rule 2.
Bare substantival adjective as an ethnic noun.
Rules 7 and 9: supplied subject with the finite verb; head on proceeded.
Rule 7: infinitival to with its verb, no conjunction governing the clause.
Rule 65's English-side test: the particle has a word of its own, also.
Second δέ realized by the second And. Textual unit SBLGNT.ACT.12.3.v002 is underdetermined between r00-base and r01 and the projection carries the base; no new textual decision is made here.
Rule 7: the supplied subject those, italicized in the ASV, is the finite verb's helper; rule 11 keeps the italics from making it added.
Rule 51's anarthrous clause: ἡμέραι carries no article, so the supplied the is an ordinary helper on the noun.

Corrected from unrepresented. Rule 102: a Greek article governs this phrase, so the supplied nominal bread is the article's and not the adjective's, and the genitive's case preposition of rides with it as it does in REV.11.15's τοῦ κυρίου -> the kingdom of; discontinuous under rule 15, headed on the supplied noun. Rule 17's generic-noun clause is scoped in terms to anarthrous Greek and does not reach a phrase an article governs, and rule 49's οἱ ἡμέτεροι -> our people shows that the article takes the nominal whether or not a determiner is written for it. This is the reading the same chapter gives τῆς βασιλικῆς -> the … country at 12.20.

Rule 102 leaves the substantival adjective its own bare word. unleavened is what glosses ἄζυμος, bread answering to no element of the lexeme — the α- is the privative and ζύμη is leaven — which is rule 66's generic-completion test and the reason the head stands on unleavened even though the supplied noun is the article's.

review_notes: Corrected: the supplied bread and the case preposition of now belong to the article under rules 102 and 49, and ἀζύμων keeps a bare unleavened. This removes the chapter's one real split, 12.20's τῆς βασιλικῆς -> the … country having already read the construction the article's way.
The head is unchanged on unleavened for the adjective's own word; what changed is which token owns the supplied noun.
The rest of the verse stands as accepted, including the split of ἀρεστόν ἐστιν into it and pleased, whose alternative the note names.
